candidates.why: Line 432 gets `name` from dwg_obj_table_get_name, which returns an INTERNAL pointer `table->name` (dwg_api.c:20931) when IS_FROM_TU_DWG(dwg) is false, but a malloc'd copy (dwg_api.c:20929) when true. The free at line 437 is guarded by IS_FROM_TU(dat) (bits.h:77, uses dat->from_version), a DIFFERENT condition than the one that decided copy-vs-internal (dwg->header.from_version). dwg_write_geojson (929-967) never syncs dat->from_version from dwg->header.from_version, so the two can diverge and line 437 can free the object's internal table->name, which is used later (e.g. dwg_geojson_feature for other objects / other writers).

Line 461 gets `name` via dwg_ent_get_ltype_name, which forwards dwg_obj_table_get_name's result: an internal `table->name` pointer when IS_FROM_TU_DWG(dwg) is false (dwg_api.c:20931), a malloc'd copy when true (dwg_api.c:20929). The free at line 466 is guarded by IS_FROM_TU(dat) (dat->from_version), not the dwg->header.from_version used to decide the copy. If dat->from_version >= R_2007 while dwg->header.from_version < R_2007, line 466 frees the ltype table's internal name, later reused by other objects/writers.

Line 574 aliases `pts = _obj->points` (the object's own array, NOT a copy). normalize_polygon_orient (582) only replaces `pts` with a new malloc'd buffer when it returns 1 (out_geojson.c:399); when it returns 0, `pts` still aliases `_obj->points`. The free at 593 is guarded by `if (changed)`, so it frees the new buffer, not _obj->points — but the aliasing at 574 makes this fragile: any future change to the guard, or a caller that reuses _obj->points after this function, would free/use the object's live points array. Worth flagging as a suspicious aliasing+free site.
